name: Kalyana Ksharam

sections.overview: Kalyana Ksharam – Benefits, Usage, Indications and Dosage
sections.introduction: Kalyana Ksharam is an ayurvedic formulation that is made up from mixture of significant herbs. This formulation is very effective in treating problems of digestion and bowel problems.
sections.ingredients:
Triphala (Haritaki – Terminalia chebula , Vibhitaki – Terminalia bellirica , Amalaki – Emblica officinalis ) 
 Trikatu (Pepper – Piper nigrum , Long pepper – Piper longum , Ginger – Zingiber officinale ) 
 Saindhava namak – Rock salt 
 Bida – Black salt 
 Samudra namak – Simple salt 
 Bhilava – Semecarpus anacardium 
 Chitraka – Plumbago zeylanica 
 Danti – Baliospermum montanum 
 Eranda taila – Castor oil 
 Cow urine 

 Method of preparation 

 Take chitraka, triphala, danti, trikatu and bhilava up to 10 grams. Take castor oil up to 80 ml and cow urine up to 160 ml. 
 Now put all the ingredients in a close container and burn to get its ash. 
 After burning process you get the kshara.
sections.dose: 125 to 500 mg for oral and external application, in different conditions, according to the prescription of the doctor.

Piles 
 Bloating 
 Constipation 
 Worm infestation 
 UTI 
 Cold 
 Stomach ache
sections.contraindications:
Over dose may cause diarrhea or burning sensations. 
 Avoid if you are taking the treatment regarding male infertility. 
 Avoid in pregnancy and lactation. 
 Avoid in case of underweight. 


 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

fullContent:
Kalyana Ksharam – Benefits, Usage, Indications and Dosage 
 Reference – Sahasrayoga Churna Prakarana 96. 
 Introduction 
 Kalyana Ksharam is an ayurvedic formulation that is made up from mixture of significant herbs. This formulation is very effective in treating problems of digestion and bowel problems. 
 Ingredients 
 
 Triphala (Haritaki – Terminalia chebula , Vibhitaki – Terminalia bellirica , Amalaki – Emblica officinalis ) 
 Trikatu (Pepper – Piper nigrum , Long pepper – Piper longum , Ginger – Zingiber officinale ) 
 Saindhava namak – Rock salt 
 Bida – Black salt 
 Samudra namak – Simple salt 
 Bhilava – Semecarpus anacardium 
 Chitraka – Plumbago zeylanica 
 Danti – Baliospermum montanum 
 Eranda taila – Castor oil 
 Cow urine 
 
 Method of preparation 
 
 Take chitraka, triphala, danti, trikatu and bhilava up to 10 grams. Take castor oil up to 80 ml and cow urine up to 160 ml. 
 Now put all the ingredients in a close container and burn to get its ash. 
 After burning process you get the kshara. 
 
 Dose 
 125 to 500 mg for oral and external application, in different conditions, according to the prescription of the doctor. 
 Indications 
 
 Piles 
 Bloating 
 Constipation 
 Worm infestation 
 UTI 
 Cold 
 Stomach ache 
 
 Contraindications 
 
 Over dose may cause diarrhea or burning sensations. 
 Avoid if you are taking the treatment regarding male infertility. 
 Avoid in pregnancy and lactation. 
 Avoid in case of underweight. 
 
 
 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.
